hook.en: You do not need a PhD, a lab or a grant to start. In twelve months, working part-time beside your normal job, you can complete a small audit, write a case report, run a pilot, present a poster and submit a paper. Small, finished projects build skill, a CV and confidence far faster than one grand plan that never ends.
hook.ur: Shuru karne ke liye PhD, lab ya grant nahi chahiye. Barah mahine mein, apni aam naukri ke saath part-time kaam karte hue, aap chhota audit mukammal, case report likh, pilot chala, poster pesh aur paper bhej sakte hain. Chhote, mukammal projects maharat, CV aur itminan ko ek bade plan se kahin tezi se banate hain jo kabhi khatam nahi hota.

goal.en: By the end, you'll follow a realistic month-by-month plan (audit, case report, pilot, poster, paper), find a mentor, protect your time, avoid common stalls and know what a good first year looks like.
goal.ur: End tak aap haqeeqat pasand mahine ba mahine plan (audit, case report, pilot, poster, paper) par chalenge, mentor dhoondhenge, apna waqt bachayenge, aam rukawaton se bachenge aur jaanenge ke achha pehla saal kaisa hota hai.

text.en: Research skills grow by **finishing small things**. A sensible first year has four blocks: **learn and plan** (a question, a mentor, ethics), **a small audit or case report** (quick to finish and publishable as a poster or short paper), **a pilot or feasibility study** (a first look at a real question, honestly small) and **sharing** (a poster, a talk, a paper submission). Most of the value comes from completing the cycle once, with feedback, rather than from the size of the project.
text.ur: Research ki maharatein **chhoti cheezein mukammal karne** se barhti hain. Samajhdar pehle saal ke chaar hisse hain: **seekhna aur plan** (sawal, mentor, ethics), **chhota audit ya case report** (jaldi mukammal aur poster ya mukhtasar paper ke taur par shaya hone ke qabil), **pilot ya feasibility study** (haqeeqi sawal par pehli nazar, imaandari se chhota) aur **share karna** (poster, talk, paper ki submission). Zyada tar faida cycle ko ek baar feedback ke saath mukammal karne se aata hai, project ke size se nahi.

text.en: Think of **learning to drive**. You do not begin on a motorway. You learn in a quiet lane, then a village road, then a main road, with an instructor beside you. Each stage is a complete trip, and by the end of a year you can drive. A first research year is the same: quiet lane (audit), village road (case report), main road (pilot).
text.ur: **Gaari chalana seekhna** sochein. Aap motorway se shuru nahi karte. Khamosh gali, phir gaon ki sadak, phir badi sadak, ustaad ke saath. Har marhala mukammal safar hai, aur saal ke aakhir tak aap chala sakte hain. Research ka pehla saal bhi aisa hi hai: khamosh gali (audit), gaon ki sadak (case report), badi sadak (pilot).

steps.title: Months 1 to 2: question, mentor, time
steps.detail: Pick a problem from your own practice, find a supervisor or mentor who has published, agree meeting times, check which approvals you need and block two protected hours a week for research. || Mahine 1 se 2: sawal, mentor, waqt

steps.title: Months 3 to 5: a small audit or case report
steps.detail: Audit ten to thirty records against a standard, or write a CARE-guided case report with consent. Aim to finish and present it. || Mahine 3 se 5: chhota audit ya case report

steps.title: Months 6 to 9: a pilot or feasibility study
steps.detail: Turn a question from the audit into a small study with a protocol, ethics approval and registration if needed. Keep it simple and honest: can it be done, and what would a larger study need? || Mahine 6 se 9: pilot ya feasibility study

steps.title: Months 10 to 12: write, present, submit
steps.detail: Write it up with the right reporting guideline, present a poster or talk at a local meeting and submit to a suitable journal after checking it is genuine. Plan the next question. || Mahine 10 se 12: likhein, pesh karein, bhejein

question.en: A new graduate wants to start with a 600-patient randomised trial in her first year, working alone. What is the best advice?
question.ur: Naya graduate pehle saal mein akele 600 mareezon ka randomised trial shuru karna chahta hai. Behtareen mashwara kya hai?

text.en: Start with a small audit or case report, finish it, learn the steps with a mentor, then build towards a pilot; a large trial needs a team, funding and experience
text.ur: Chhote audit ya case report se shuru karein, mukammal karein, mentor ke saath qadam seekhein, phir pilot ki taraf barhein; bare trial ko team, funding aur tajurba chahiye

feedback.en: Yes — finishing small projects builds the skills for larger ones.
feedback.ur: Haan — chhote projects mukammal karna bade projects ki maharat banata hai.

text.en: Go ahead alone, because ambition matters most
text.ur: Akele shuru karein, kyunke ambition sab se ahem hai

feedback.ur: Ghair haqeeqi ambitious projects aksar ruk jate hain.

text.en: Do nothing until a grant arrives
text.ur: Grant aane tak kuch na karein

feedback.ur: Chhote projects ko kam paisa chahiye.

question.en: Why is it useful to find a mentor who has published?
question.ur: Aisa mentor dhoondhna jis ne chhapa ho mufeed kyun hai?

text.en: They know the practical steps, can warn you about pitfalls, and can help with ethics, writing and journals, which saves months
text.ur: Woh amali qadam jaante hain, jaal se khabardar kar sakte hain, aur ethics, likhne aur journals mein madad kar sakte hain, jo mahine bachata hai

feedback.en: Yes — experience shortens the learning curve.
feedback.ur: Haan — tajurba seekhne ka waqt kam karta hai.

text.en: To have someone else do the work

feedback.en: A mentor guides; you do the work.
feedback.ur: Mentor rehnumai karta hai; kaam aap karte hain.

text.en: To add a famous name for free
text.ur: Muft mein mashhoor naam jorne ke liye

question.en: Your audit finds that only half of patients had a falls-risk check. What should you do next?
question.ur: Aap ka audit paata hai ke sirf aadhe mareezon ka girne ke khatre ka check hua. Aap ko agla kya karna chahiye?

text.en: File the result and move on
text.ur: Nateeja file karein aur aage barhein

feedback.en: An audit without change helps no one.
feedback.ur: Tabdeeli ke baghair audit kisi ki madad nahi karta.

text.en: Share the result without blame, agree one small change with colleagues, try it for a few weeks and re-audit
text.ur: Bina ilzam ke nateeja share karein, saathiyon ke saath ek chhoti tabdeeli tay karein, chand haftay aazmayein aur dobara audit karein

feedback.en: Yes — closing the loop turns an audit into improvement and a presentable project.
feedback.ur: Haan — chakkar band karna audit ko behtari aur pesh karne ke qabil project banata hai.

text.en: Blame the colleagues who missed it
text.ur: Jinhon ne chhoda un ko ilzam dein

text.en: **Starting big, working alone, and never finishing.** Many promising clinicians begin an ambitious project, lose momentum when the clinic gets busy and end the year with nothing to show. Choose a size you can finish in months, protect weekly time, set dates with your mentor and celebrate completion. A finished small study is worth far more than a half-finished large one.
text.ur: **Bade se shuru karna, akele kaam karna aur kabhi mukammal na karna.** Bohat se ummeed afza clinicians ambitious project shuru karte hain, clinic masroof hone par raftar kho dete hain aur saal bina kuch dikhaye khatam karte hain. Aisa size chunein jo mahinon mein mukammal ho, haftawar waqt mehfooz rakhein, mentor ke saath tareekhein tay karein aur mukammal karne ka jashn manayein. Mukammal chhota study adhoore bare study se kahin qeemti hai.

text.en: **Make it visible and shared.** Put your timeline on the wall, tell your clinic colleagues what you are doing and invite one of them to join. Present a five-minute update at your team meeting each month. A small group, even two or three people, keeps projects alive far better than willpower alone, and shares the credit and the work.
text.ur: **Isay nazar aane wala aur mushtarak banayein.** Apni timeline deewar par lagayein, clinic ke saathiyon ko batayein aap kya kar rahe hain aur ek ko shamil hone ki dawat dein. Har mahine team meeting mein paanch minute ka update dein. Chhota group, do ya teen log bhi, projects ko irade se kahin behtar zinda rakhta hai aur credit aur kaam baant-ta hai.

question.en: What does a "good" first year of research look like?
question.ur: Research ka "achha" pehla saal kaisa lagta hai?

answer.en: It looks modest: one completed audit with a re-audit, one case report or poster, a draft of a pilot protocol or a small pilot, a talk at a local meeting and one manuscript under review or in preparation. More importantly, you now have a mentor, a habit of weekly work, an understanding of ethics and reporting, and a question for year two.
answer.ur: Yeh saada lagta hai: ek mukammal audit re-audit ke saath, ek case report ya poster, pilot ke protocol ka draft ya chhota pilot, muqami mulaqat mein ek talk aur ek manuscript jo review mein ya tayyari mein ho. Is se zyada ahem, ab aap ke paas mentor, haftawar kaam ki aadat, ethics aur reporting ki samajh aur doosre saal ke liye ek sawal hai.

beats.patient: A physiotherapist in a district hospital wants to do research but has no funding and little time. She picks one question: how many stroke patients get a standard shoulder-positioning check. She finds a mentor at a nearby university.
beats.assessment: An audit is realistic: no funding, little time, and it can lead to change.
beats.treatment: She audits 30 records, finds a 40 percent completion rate, introduces a one-page checklist, re-audits after eight weeks (now 80 percent), presents a poster and then plans a pilot study of carer training.
beats.reassess: Within the year she has a poster, a quality improvement paper under review, a mentor and a clear next question.

text.en: **Keep patients and your job safe.** Do the work in ways that do not reduce care or add risk. Get approval from your employer and, where needed, an ethics committee. Do not collect extra data from patients without consent, and do not let research time take over clinical duties. If you feel overloaded, tell your mentor early and shrink the project.
text.ur: **Mareezon aur apni naukri ko mehfooz rakhein.** Kaam aise karein jo care kam na karein ya khatra na barhayen. Apne employer aur zaroorat par ethics committee se manzoori lein. Mareezon se razamandi ke baghair mazeed data jama na karein, aur research ka waqt clinical farayez par haavi na hone dein. Agar bojh mehsoos ho to mentor ko jaldi batayein aur project chhota karein.

text.en: Chalmers and Glasziou estimated that a large share of research investment is wasted through poorly chosen questions, inadequate design, unpublished results and unusable reports, and argued that careful question selection, good methods and full reporting are the most effective ways to add value. SQUIRE 2.0 supports small improvement projects by setting out how to report them so that others can learn from and repeat them, which is why audit and quality improvement are practical first projects for busy clinicians.
text.ur: Chalmers aur Glasziou ne andaaza lagaya ke research ki sarmaya-kari ka bara hissa kharab chune gaye sawalon, na-kaafi design, ghair shaya shuda nateejon aur na-qabil-e-istemal reports se zaya hota hai, aur daleel di ke sawal ka ehtiyat se intikhab, achhe tareeqe aur mukammal report qeemat barhane ke sab se mu'assir tareeqe hain. SQUIRE 2.0 chhote behtari ke projects ki is tarah madad karta hai ke un ki report kaise di jaye taake doosre seekh aur dohra saken, isi liye audit aur quality improvement masroof clinicians ke liye amali pehle projects hain.

text.en: **Mentor, Small, Finish, Share.** Find a mentor, start small, finish what you start and share it.
text.ur: **Mentor, Chhota, Mukammal, Share.** Mentor dhoondhein, chhote se shuru karein, jo shuru karein mukammal karein aur share karein.

summary.en: A good first research year is a cycle of small finished projects: audit, case report, pilot, poster and paper.
summary.ur: Research ka achha pehla saal chhote mukammal projects ka chakkar hai: audit, case report, pilot, poster aur paper.

summary.en: Find a published mentor, protect weekly time and choose a size you can finish.
summary.ur: Chhapa hua mentor dhoondhein, haftawar waqt mehfooz rakhein aur aisa size chunein jo mukammal ho sake.

summary.en: Keep patients safe, get approvals and never trade finishing for ambition.
summary.ur: Mareezon ko mehfooz rakhein, manzooriyan lein aur ambition ke liye mukammal karna kabhi na chhorein.
